page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache allocations include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside vector processing via standard AVX, though advanced extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are absent.

Benchmark measurements indicate robust multi-threaded CPU throughput, scoring 86,222.56 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 61,840.51 on PassMark CPU evaluations, both placing in the top quartile. Cryptographic throughput is similarly elevated, reaching 68,414.08 on PassMark CPU encryption tests. The memory architecture registers 4,074.06 GB/sec under cached 16 KB read workloads, paired with an overall PassMark memory score of 2,886.74. In-memory data structures perform exceptionally well, evidenced by Redis throughput reaching 63.14 million SET operations per second and strong PassMark database operations scores. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into median ranges, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,571.0 and static web serving throughput measuring 35.39 GB/sec.

The instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, requiring persistent disk attachments for persistent state. Large language model inference reveals execution tradeoffs typical of CPU-only hardware: text generation on a 135M model achieves a strong 297.57 tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly to 26.12 tokens per second on 7B models and falls into the bottom decile at 2.41 tokens per second on 70B models. In terms of cost efficiency, the AMD EPYC platform provides high compute core density and solid parallel integer performance per resource allocation, making it well-suited for high-concurrency backend services, large relational or in-memory databases, multi-threaded data processing, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 AMD EPYC 7B13 physical cores and 256 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture, it preserves a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, supplemented by hardware cryptographic acceleration including AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-quartile multi-threaded performance, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 61,840.51, a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,971.0, and 63.14 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core processing and large-scale LLM generation remain in median to lower performance brackets. The hardware profile offers balanced compute density, making it suited for enterprise database hosting, distributed in-memory caching, backend application clusters, and parallel build pipelines.
